## Question

How does body mass vary across Adelie, Chinstrap, and Gentoo penguins??? Hmm let's see.

## Data source

Data: [Palmer Penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/),
collected by Dr. Kristen Gorman and Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.
The data are available under a CC0 license.

## Load the data

```{python}
#| label: load-data

from palmerpenguins import load_penguins

penguins = load_penguins()
penguins.head()
```

## Check data quality

Before comparing species, I check the dataset size and count missing
values in the variables needed for this analysis.

```{python}
#| label: check-missing-values

print(f"Number of rows: {penguins.shape[0]}")
penguins[["species", "body_mass_g"]].isna().sum()
```

## Prepare the data

Two observations have missing body mass (Na). I exclude these two rows from the
comparison and keep observations with missing values in unrelated columns.

```{python}
#| label: remove-missing-mass

penguins_clean = penguins.dropna(subset=["body_mass_g"]).copy()

print(f"Original rows: {len(penguins)}")
print(f"Rows retained: {len(penguins_clean)}")
print(f"Rows removed: {len(penguins) - len(penguins_clean)}")
```

## Compare body mass across species

I calculate the number of observations, mean, and median body mass
for each species. Body mass is measured in grams.

```{python}
#| label: summarize-body-mass

mass_summary = (
    penguins_clean.groupby("species")["body_mass_g"]
    .agg(["count", "mean", "median"])
    .round(1)
)

mass_summary
```

## Findings :O

Gentoo penguins have the highest mean body mass in this sample:
approximately 5,076 g, compared with 3,701 g for Adelie and
3,733 g for Chinstrap. The median follows the same pattern:
5,000 g for Gentoo and 3,700 g for both other species.

These are descriptive comparisons of the observed penguins.
They do not establish that species alone explains the differences;
this analysis does not account for factors such as sex, island, or year.
Two observations with missing body mass were excluded.

## Visualize body mass

The boxplot compares the median, spread, and potential outliers
of body mass across species.

```{python}
#| label: fig-body-mass
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of body mass by species, excluding two observations with missing body mass."

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

species = ["Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo"]
mass_by_species = [
    penguins_clean.loc[
        penguins_clean["species"] == name, "body_mass_g"
    ]
    for name in species
]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
ax.boxplot(mass_by_species, tick_labels=species)
ax.set_xlabel("Species")
ax.set_ylabel("Body mass (g)")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
